summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as a one-armed load balancer: TCP port 80 on its LAN/management address (10.100.6.10) round-robins to node2 and node3's HTTP servers on port 8080 via a pf rdr-to pool rule plus a matching outbound SNAT rule that masquerades traffic to the backends as coming from node1 (required because backend replies otherwise bypassed NAT translation and returned directly to the client — an asymmetric routing issue). Verified node4 receives alternating responses identifying node2 and node3 through the single port-80 entry point. Also disabled OPNsense's automatic HTTP->HTTPS webgui redirect (disablehttpredirect) since it owned port 80 via an anti-lockout no-rdr rule that shadowed the new DNAT rule. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all 4 nodes with captured baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery verification for each.
actions_performed: Inspected all 4 nodes; identified node1 as OPNsense (FreeBSD) single-homed on the shared 10.100.6.0/24 LAN with node2/node3/node4
Studied OPNsense's MVC firewall models (DNat, Filter/snatrules, Alias) directly on the box to determine current config syntax
Created a host alias 'lb_backends' (10.100.6.11, 10.100.6.12) via the OPNsense Alias model
Added a DNAT (port-forward) rule: lan:80/tcp -> lb_backends:8080 with poolopts=round-robin and pass=pass
Found and fixed a port-80 anti-lockout no-rdr rule blocking the forward by setting system.webgui.disablehttpredirect

Diagnosed an asymmetric-routing failure (backend SYN-ACK bypassing NAT) via tcpdump on node1/node2/node3; fixed by adding a manual outbound SNAT rule masquerading LB->backend traffic to the LAN interface address
Deployed systemd-managed Python HTTP servers on node2 and node3 serving hostname-identifying content on port 8080, opened firewalld port 8080/tcp on both
Verified end-to-end round-robin load balancing from node4 through node1:80 to both backends

Executed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol on node2, node3, node4 (systemctl reboot) and node1 (shutdown -r now), capturing baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart service/data recovery for each, verifying full LB functionality after every restart

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 serve HTTP on 8080 identifying the host
evidence.summary: Deployed and verified systemd HTTP servers on node2 (10.100.6.11) and node3 (10.100.6.12) each returning 'Hello from <hostname>'

evidence.requirement: node1 presents one entry point on TCP 80 of its management address that spreads requests across both hosts
evidence.summary: Built and applied OPNsense DNAT rule with round-robin pool to lb_backends alias on lan:80; confirmed active in pfctl -s nat

evidence.requirement: Diagnosed and fixed port-80 anti-lockout conflict blocking the forward
evidence.summary: curl showed OPNsense webgui intercepting port 80 with a 301 redirect; disabled disablehttpredirect and confirmed no-rdr rule for http was removed

evidence.requirement: Diagnosed and fixed asymmetric NAT routing so backend replies return via node1
evidence.summary: tcpdump proved backend SYN-ACKs bypassed node1 and reached the client directly (dropped); added outbound SNAT rule masquerading LB->backend traffic; confirmed NAT rule active

evidence.requirement: node4 receives answers from each host through the port-80 entry point
evidence.summary: node4 curl to http://10.100.6.10:80/ returned alternating 'Hello from node2'/'Hello from node3' responses across repeated requests

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 45c22b1f...; reboot acknowledged then connection dropped; polled back up with new boot_id 6149200c... and lb-backend/firewalld active, content served

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f7db4b4e...; reboot acknowledged and disconnected; polled back up with new boot_id d2952a1d...; services recovered and round-robin confirmed with both backends

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id df8bab0d...; reboot acknowledged and disconnected; polled back up with new boot_id fb4a8d86...; immediately confirmed round-robin still functions post-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery of LB config and function
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime sec=1788626955; shutdown -r now acknowledged, SSH connection subsequently timed out confirming disruption; polled back up; kern.boottime changed to sec=1788627799 (uptime 9s) proving reboot; pf NAT/rdr rules persisted from config.xml and full round-robin load balancing verified end-to-end from node4
